model.rationale: LaHood combines an 11-point Republican district lean with a hundred-to-one cash advantage over Nolley, and prediction markets price his re-election near 96 percent; the Democratic-tilted national environment narrows the expected margin somewhat but leaves the race far from competitive.
model.watch: Any public polling showing Nolley within single digits, or significant outside spending entering the district against LaHood, would warrant revisiting the forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Darin LaHood seeks another term in a central Illinois district drawn with an 11-point Republican lean. He has raised $4.2 million and holds nearly $6 million on hand, while Democrat Paul Nolley has about $59,000 available after raising $639,000. No outside groups are advertising in the race, and no public general-election polls have been conducted.

Prediction markets give LaHood roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. The national political environment leans Democratic this cycle, which narrows the district's structural advantage somewhat but leaves a wide gap. With a heavily funded incumbent, a lopsided financial disparity, and no polling indicating competition, LaHood is a clear favorite, though the absence of survey data keeps uncertainty wider than in well-polled races.
